sections.content:
You know the concessive future (*será caro, pero…*) and evaluative *con lo … que* / *para lo … que* from C1 Unit 20, and ironic *ni que* + imperfect subjunctive from C1 Unit 21. Using these three constructions well is a hallmark of an agile, personal voice: they let you concede a point, evaluate expectations and add light humour.

The **concessive future** grants a fact before countering it with *pero*: *Tendrá sus dificultades, pero merece la pena*. ***Con lo* + adj./adv. + *que*** highlights a surprising contrast (*Con lo difícil que parecía, al final lo dominaste*), while ***para lo* + adj. + *que*** measures something against what you would expect (*Para lo corto que es, dice mucho*).

***¡Ni que* + imperfect subjunctive!*** rejects an exaggeration playfully or ironically (*¡Ni que fuera tan complicado!* — 'as if it were that complicated!').

sections.title: Stance, evaluation & irony
rows: *Será exigente, pero te da una voz ágil.* ('It may be demanding, but…')
*Con lo largo que era el borrador, lo resumiste muy bien.*
*Para lo poco que practicó, habla con gran soltura.*
*¡Ni que tuviéramos que memorizar el diccionario entero!*

items.spanish: Tendrá fama de difícil, pero dominar estos giros te permite alternar registros con humor.
items.english: It may have a reputation for being difficult, but mastering these turns lets you alternate registers with humour.

items.spanish: Con lo tímida que era al principio, ahora debate con una agilidad admirable.
items.english: Considering how shy she was at first, she now debates with admirable agility.

items.spanish: Para lo breve que fue la nota, creó una complicidad inmediata con la sala.
items.english: For how brief the note was, it created immediate rapport with the room.

items.spanish: ¡Ni que un pequeño desliz fuera el fin del mundo!
items.english: As if a small slip were the end of the world!

sections.content: After ironic *ni que*, use the **imperfect subjunctive** (or the pluperfect for a completed past event): *¡Ni que fuera fácil!*, never indicative *¡Ni que es fácil!* or present subjunctive *¡Ni que sea fácil!*). And remember the adjective inside *con lo … que* agrees with its subject (*con lo larga que es la lista*).
